summary: Five Finger Light, at the entrance to Stephens Passage, was one of Alaska's first two U.S. lighthouses (1 March 1902); fire destroyed the wooden original in 1933 and a concrete station replaced it in 1935.

access.note: Reached only by boat, plane or helicopter; no overnight moorage; run by the Five Finger Lighthouse Society with volunteers.

corrections.why: The record gives a concrete tower built 1902; the nomination and the Bulletin show the 1902 building was wooden and the concrete one dates from 1934-35.

corrections.proposed: none; the light is still active
corrections.why: The nomination says the Coast Guard continues to service the light and the 2023 Pilot describes the navigational light; 1998 appears to be an archive field and does not match any source for a closure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says Congress appropriated $22,500 for the light; the Light-House Board's 1901 report shows $22,500 was the lowest bid accepted, against an estimate of $32,900.
The Bulletin reports a boathouse destroyed by fire on 19 May 1927, but the nomination and the Society call the boathouse an original 1902 building that survived the 1933 fire. Not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: One newspaper search (Chronicling America, 1902-05) was run; the Skagway Daily Morning Alaskan of 8 Feb 1903 confirms the Amur episode in outline but differs from Lighthouse Friends (no January date, no flour and fish, 'three months' absence of one man, supplies were sugar, tobacco and vegetables). The OCR of that page is poor. The 1933 fire details of the frozen pipe and blowtorch are also Lighthouse Friends only. Lighthouse Board annual reports after 1901 are not in the corpus, so no fiscal-year report is cited for fog-signal hours or the first years. The Bulletin dates: the 1927 item is in the 1 August 1927 issue (events of May to July 1927); the 1933 rescue item is in the 1 May 1933 issue; its exact rescue date is not given. The fire item in the 2 January 1934 Bulletin is on printed page 168. Hall's efficiency pennant/flag rests on Bulletin index entries (1912-17 p.147, 1918-23 p.78) plus Lighthouse Friends; the underlying Bulletin text was not read. Bulletin 1918 p.23 is the PDF page. OCR'd Bulletin columns in the 1934 fire item interleave, so quotes were picked from single runs. Names matched by position: none from tables; roster lines are copied from the archive page. USLHS gives Kashevaroff 1936-1938, Lighthouse Friends 1936-1939, and Lighthouse Friends lists Ray K. Dell (1936) as head keeper, not in the archive. The Society's lighthouse page says the present building was constructed in 1933; the nomination says 1934-35 and the Bulletin 1937 says 1935. The USLHS place record says discontinued 1998, which conflicts with an active light. The nomination gives 37 miles from Petersburg; Lighthouse Friends says 41 miles. The nomination says '18-mile range' and a focal plane of 81 feet; range not used. The Society volunteer page opening dates are undated (2018-era posts).
